title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 15
paragraphs: Xerxes, badly shaken by fear of the vision, sprang up from his bed and sent a messenger to summon Artabanus. When Artabanus came, Xerxes said: “Artabanus, at first I was not sensible: I spoke foolish words to you on account of your good counsel. But not long afterwards I changed my mind and realized that I should do the things you suggested. I am unable to do them now, however, eager though I am; for ever since I turned around and changed my mind, a dream has been haunting me and utterly disapproving of my new course, and just now it has left me with a threat. If, then, it is God who sends this dream, and it is his absolute will and pleasure that an army should march against Greece, this same dream will come flying to you too, laying the same charge on you as it has on me. It occurs to me that this might happen if you were to take all my royal clothing and put it on, sit on my throne, and then lie down to sleep in my bed.”
